### Historical audit — S0188

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/service_incident_01/retired/results/r1/generic_rsi/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines and decoded-observation character ranges.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student model request, line 1, [0,10096) | The assigned goal was reconstruction of an indoor RGB photograph using separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching camera, framing, occlusion, colors and materials. The image was supplied by path, but its pixels are not visible in this audit; specific scene contents cannot be established. The requested workflow included a first complete build and render-based revision. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 2, [0,2623) | One fresh, read-only CLI session was launched with the staged image. It failed with exit code 1 after about 19.84 seconds; the record reports zero tool calls. No student program, scene change, Blender execution, render, or autonomous exploration is visible. |
| Student `model_error` and `scene_error`, lines 3 [0,544) and 4 [0,1606) | The request propagated a runtime error because Codex exited 1. The trace points to a stderr log but does not include its contents, so the underlying cause is unknown. |

**Scene checks and validation:** The prompt required multiple objects and separate parts, materials, camera and lighting, but the visible record contains no constructed objects or render. Consequently, object multiplicity, material or texture fidelity, part connections, pose, camera, lighting and render quality are **unverified**, not demonstrated failures. There is no visible independent visual or geometric validation.

**Teacher and outcome:** No teacher input, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, execution, or adoption is visible. This is a student trajectory, not a teacher-only trace. The supported classification is **technical interruption before a visible build**; reconstruction correctness and any eventual outcome are unknown. An empty patch or algorithmic failure is not established.

**Transferable lesson and uncertainty:** A failed model invocation is not evidence about reconstruction quality; diagnosing it requires the actual stderr or other execution evidence. The particular service failure and any image-specific modeling issues remain unresolved hypotheses.
